tytul: Pickled elder buds and green elderberries: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for green elder flower buds or unripe elderberries pickled in vinegar after heating, sometimes called elder capers. [T:-]

ostrzezenia.tekst: According to Ask Extension, it is dangerous to eat unripe elderberries or any other parts of the plant, such as stems, leaves and bark; raw, unripe berries and other parts of the plant contain compounds that can become poisonous. [T:ACI-450]

According to Ask Extension, known elderberry poisonings have been traced to leaves in the product or to unripe berries; only fully ripe berries should be processed or eaten, with all stems, leaves and unripe berries removed. [T:ACI-451]

akapity: In a study of American elderberry, the total cyanogenic potential was highest in the stems and in unripe (green) berries, and the authors advise separating stems, green berries and leaves from ripe berries when preparing products. [T:ACI-453]
Oregon State University Extension advises harvesting elderberries when the fruit is fully ripe. [T:ACI-452]
JarAtlas has found no checked source showing that heating or pickling makes green elder buds or unripe elderberries safe to eat. [T:-]
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for pickled elder buds or unripe elderberries from a checked source. [T:-]
